verification.summary: The ACCS script skips two explicit accs.md checks — the zero-comments state right after mock startup, and that already-loaded issues other than #1 end up with exactly 1 comment — so a broken tracker or broken initial state could still pass.

mustFix.quote: echo "$EARLY" | grep -q '\[' || fail 'issues endpoint did not return a list'
mustFix.problem: accs.md says to ensure issues exist 'but all of them without any comments' right after mock startup. The script only checks the response is a list, never checking comment counts are zero, so a mock that seeds issues with comments already attached would still pass.

mustFix.quote: echo "$LAST_BLOCK" | grep -q '^Issue #1: (2)' || fail 'issue #1 does not have 2 comments after tracker run'
mustFix.problem: accs.md requires checking that the first issue has 2 comments AND the rest of the already-loaded issues have exactly 1. Only issue #1 is checked here, so a tracker that skips or double-comments on other issues would still pass ACCS.

shouldFix.problem: The enriched spec's 'Decisions already made' explicitly states accs.md curls without an author to exercise the Anonymous default, but the script sends an explicit author, so that documented rationale doesn't match what's actually tested.

shouldFix.quote: echo "$LAST_BLOCK" | grep -q 'I..ve been here!' || echo "$LAST_BLOCK" | grep -q "been here" || fail 'no I have been here comment found'
shouldFix.problem: This only checks the phrase appears somewhere in the last block, not that each other already-loaded issue individually got exactly one such comment, so it can't catch a tracker that only comments on one issue.

shouldKnow.quote: MAKE SURE THAT ONLY THE MOCK INSTANCES ARE BEING USED!
shouldKnow.problem: Neither accs.md nor accs.bash actually verifies this beyond using the mock-github command by convention; there's no assertion (e.g. env var check) that a real GitHub token/endpoint isn't in play, left as an unenforced assumption.
